finding.claim: Unauthenticated remote attacker can run arbitrary shell commands as the Node.js process user via the host query parameter of GET /ping, and the command output is returned in the HTTP response (CRITICAL).
finding.source: req.query.host on GET /ping (tools.js:6), an unauthenticated query parameter.
finding.sink: child_process.exec() at tools.js:7, which runs the concatenated string through /bin/sh.

trace.note: app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds all interfaces, so the route is public ingress.
app.get('/ping') route is registered with no auth middleware.
req.query.host is concatenated into 'ping -c 1 ' and passed to exec(), which runs a shell.
stdout of the injected command is returned to the client via res.send(out) on success.

finding.guards_checked: None present. No input validation, allowlist, shell escaping, or argument-array execFile. No authentication or authorization middleware on the route. No WAF or rate limit in code. Deployment-level firewalling was not verifiable (Bash disabled, no network checks). Triage Check 13 answered affirmatively on all five questions. Semgrep passes were skipped.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6-7 passes req.query.host unvalidated into string concatenation for exec(), which runs through /bin/sh. There is no allowlist, escaping, or execFile argument array. No auth middleware is registered on /ping (tools.js:6). Output is returned at tools.js:11. The only other listener is app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28, with no host argument. Deployment firewalling is not visible in the repo and could not be verified.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: /ping at tools.js:6 has no auth, the unescaped req.query.host is concatenated into exec() at tools.js:7, stdout is returned at tools.js:11, and app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 binds without a host, so an anonymous remote attacker can reach it and no in-code control blocks injection.
